doc.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025

title: The clave inside Afro-Cuban musicians, and playing it with the foot
summary: Rowe praises a video of Conte playing 3-2 clave with his foot; Conte explains the clave is internalized by anyone raised in the culture, even when nobody plays it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Earlier today I caught a video of you – I think you might have made it for your website, I’m not sure. But it started off with you sitting in front of three conga drums and you were playing the 3-2 clave with your left foot, and then you started doing your thing on the congas. And I just wanted to point out that I really enjoyed it.

Oh thank you. Yeah. You know because all that Cuban – if I’m playing congas and I’m playing authentic Cuban rhythms it all relates to the clave you know that. So I figured do a little bit of independence, put the clave in the foot and do that. I’m not the only guy that does that, a lot of the younger guys do that all the time. You know.

Years ago I was doing an educational thing with a Latin band from Albany, New York and we were trying to prepare the students to hear them. And the teacher says well – and the clave of course came up. And I was listening to the band and sometimes I’m going where is it? No one is playing it in this particular song but I assume it’s still there in your mind?

Yeah it’s inside. If you grew up in that culture with that music, the clave is inside of you. It’s there. And we know, it doesn’t necessarily have to be a percussionist, you know the pianist – every one of us playing knows where it is. If they know this music you know, they really understand the music, the culture. It’s just a thing. It may be, you know, if we didn’t have a drummer right know and a bass player and a guitar player start playing some real funky stuff, you immediately go to [claps] two and four. It’s inside of you. You have to. To us, to the Afro-Cuban drummer and musician, the clave is that. It’s just like automatic you know.
